author: zhangbo2012
body:
Mac/Extras.install.py，Can not filter osx DS_store file

As 

```python
if name == '.DS_store': return 0
```

But in OSX, Real File Name is ` .DS_Store`, like this

```shell
(venv) zhangbo@zhangbodeMacBook-Pro a2 % ll -a
total 16
drwxr-xr-x  4 zhangbo  staff   128 Oct 22 17:34 .
drwxr-xr-x  8 zhangbo  staff   256 Oct 22 17:18 ..
-rw-r--r--@ 1 zhangbo  staff  6148 Oct 22 17:17 .DS_Store
drwxr-xr-x  3 zhangbo  staff    96 Oct 22 17:23 123
```

So we need update `.DS_store` to `.DS_Store`

author: bredelings
body:
This PR is a start on cleaning up tree summaries.

It does a few different things:
1. Minimize the number of times that we copy trees to insert them into a tree trace.  Creating and destroying nodes for trees is quite slow.
2. Check that trees in the same trace have the same set of taxa -- the same TaxonMap.
3. Give understandable error messages when trees have different taxa.  Previously we were saying something like `Two nodes had same index of '144'`.  That doesn't help identify the source of the problem.
4. Include tip taxa AND sampled ancestors in the taxon set.
5. Avoid recompiling most of RevBayes when the TraceTree.h and TreeSummary.h files change.
6. Fix computePairwiseRFDistance

The PR is preparatory for further changes in TreeSummary.  Eventually, we should check that all the trees in the trace have the same set of (tips + sampled ancestors), and assign those taxa the same index in every tree.

author: andremissaglia
body:
In a normal situation, `h.gotConn` ends with:

```
stats.ConnBegin
stats.ConnBegin
stats.ConnEnd
stats.ConnEnd
```

But with the current waiting algorithm, this situation would be enough to stop waiting:
```
stats.ConnBegin
stats.ConnBegin
stats.ConnEnd
```
And the test fails with 
```
stats_test.go:1421: h.gotConn: unexpected amount of ConnStats: 3 != 4
```

I was able to reproduce this behavior with the following command. After the fix, the tests passed:
```
go test -count=10000  -run 'Test/MultipleClientStatsHandler' ./stats
```

Fixes #5695 

RELEASE NOTES: N/A

- [ ] Verify that (GitHub thinks) the merge is clean. If it isn't, and you're confident you can resolve the conflicts, do so. Otherwise, send it back to the original developer.
- [ ] Verify that the related Jira ticket exists and has a target version number and that it is correct.

- [ ] Verify that the branch destination of the PR matches the target version of the ticket

- [ ] Check for version history, if needed
- [ ] Check BaTLab dashboard for successful build (https://batlab.chtc.wisc.edu/results/workspace.php) and test for either the PR or a workspace build by the developer that has the Jira ticket as a comment.
- [ ] Check that each commit message references the Jira ticket (HTCONDOR-xxx)

## After the above

- Assign JIRA Ticket back to the developer

body:
#### 6c434b5464a00be355e52531b1d20d2637e2b295 
Computed value CSS gradients need to serialize colors in their computed form
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=246927

Reviewed by Darin Adler.

Converts StyleGradientImage to store color stop colors as StyleColors rather
than keeping the primitive values. This is the intended model of the Style
classes (storing Style types rather than CSS types) and is now possible that
the spec requires that the computed value not maintain the specified values
(e.g. we use `rgb(255, 0, 0)` and not `red` if `red` was specified).

   ### 3.3.2

   ### 3.3.1

   ```
bpo-42043: Add tests capturing subclassing requirements.
   ```

   ### 3.3.0
   ```
   ======

9: ``Path`` objects now expose a ``.filename`` attribute
and rely on that to resolve ``.name`` and ``.parent`` when
the ``Path`` object is at the root of the zipfile.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.0
   ```
   ======

57 and bpo-40564: Mutate the passed ZipFile object
type instead of making a copy. Prevents issues when
both the local copy and the caller's copy attempt to
close the same file handle.

56 and bpo-41035: ``Path._next`` now honors
subclasses.
   ```

<!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: -->

- [ ] Hot fix (emergency fix and release)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Documentation (change which affects the documentation site)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Release (`develop` -> `main`)

## Quality assurance (all should be covered).

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] Documentation for my change is up to date?
- [x] My PR meets testing requirements.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.
- [x] All commits are signed-off.

## Summary
Improved the check for model equivalence to recurse and check every attribute except specified ones.
Converted references to __field_set__ to __field__ because field_set only pertains to fields set when the obect was first initialized.  other fields could be set later and they would be missed.
## Key links:

- [Sonar coverage](https://sonarcloud.io/dashboard?id=compliance-trestle)

# Before you merge

- Ensure it is a 'squash commit' if not a release.
- Ensure CI is currently passing
- Check sonar. If you are working for a fork a maintainer will reach out, if required.

author: anuraaga
body:
- Replace TinyGo GC with one that uses malloc for backing pages instead of taking ownership of heap
- Use mimalloc as malloc implementation

The GC currently has a fixed size heap for Go. It is able to go through an entire run of FTW without crashing out-of-memory, so we may have a steady-state not going over the limit but I will improve this going forward.

`gc` package is mostly copied from TinyGo, replacing `initHeap` with `init` and use of malloc instead of wasm heap operations and some `go:linkname` to allow things to link into TinyGo

author: sskii
body:
We made the following tweaks to the config in our team and found them useful. I don't know how useful they would be for the bare-bones class template, but I'll suggest them anyway.

### Separate environments
PlatformIO allows rapid switching between compilation environments using the bottom ribbon. Using seperate environments for debug (the ~P chip) and Xplained (the ~PB chip) is more convenient than changing the config file back and forth. It also makes it easy to build both, and eliminates the opportunity to build the wrong one (they'll make different files).

### Enable all warnings
We did this and it caught several bugs at compilation time. Warnings aren't everyone's cup of tea, but this is an easy way to enable them.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: unorderedsigh
body:
With these changes, the Hai Reveal campaign should be playable from start to finish. Some of these bugs made it unplayable, others caused glitches, and there are a few textual corrections. Thanks to @MasterOfGrey who provided some fixes and a detailed review, and to @NomadicVolcano and @Hurleveur for advice.

There are four problems I didn't fix, which cause parts of the campaign to not work as intended, but it does still work.

## Testing Done

Played entire game from the beginning, passing through Free Worlds Reconciliation, Hai Reveal, to the beginning of the Wanderers. Also, I obtained Coalition and Remnant outfits licenses to test new ship designs. I did this without meeting the Hai until the message.

For my third set of fixes, I replayed a few more ways:

1. Meet the Hai but  not the Unfettered, and start the campaign.
2. Meet both Hai factions, and start the campaign.
3. Go through the red wormhole. This bypasses a long sequence of missions.

Also, I ran all of the hai reveal files through a spell checker.

## Fix Details

### Things Not Fixed

These problems cause the campaign to not work as intended, but you can still play through the campaign:

1. Hai Reveal [A14] A Time of Trouble - escort randomly-chosen ships that may not have enough fuel. This seams reasonable to me; this is *not* an early game escort mission. Helping a ship with too little fuel is an okay added challenge. 
2. Pincer Beasts cannot keep up with asteroids in some systems. They just wiggle around trying to keep up until they get bored and leave. It's very cute, but (according to NomadicVolcano) it was not the intent. Reverse thrusters and stronger forward thrusters would help.
3. Hai Reveal [B02] Join the Fleet - fails when a ship with "npc accompany" dies, even if it does not have "save." Something in the engine isn't working how it should. My workaround is to remove "accompany" until someone fixes this.
4. Hai Reveal [A07] Deliver the Relays - relays remain in your cargo hold, so you fail if they don't return to Earth. I contrived an excuse: you're returning the deployment hardware.

The "Remnant: Defense 3" mission also deploys satellites, so I'm pinging @Zitchas who may have a solution.

### First Batch of Fixes

The initial fixes before the PR was reviewed:

1. Hai Reveal: Reputation Reset - change Philosophers government to Elenctic Commune
2. Yeertle Hint - wrong type of `"` led to mission description being incomplete
3. hai_reveal_2_intro - three missions used ": Offered" instead of ": offered" for variable names, causing missions to never complete
5. Hai Building Mountaintop [2] Recruits - removed angle braces
6. Hai Reveal [A03a] Symbol Identification - removed angle braces
7. Hai Reveal [A04] Report to Teeneep - mission was never offered due to incorrect source and missing `event: ` in the "to offer" block
8. Hai Reveal [A05] Take Teeneep to Hai-home - mission was never offered due to missing `event: ` in the "to offer" block
9. Hai Reveal [A06a] The Calm - grammar error
10. Hai Reveal [A07] Deliver the Relays description - changed an incorrect/confusing mission description
11. Hai Reveal [A07] Deliver the Relays conversation - removed angle brackets and corrected indentation
12. Hai Reveal [A08] Symbol Identification - proper nouns should be capitalized. Also, this is consistent with other places the Navy Intelligence Observatory is mentioned
13. Hai Reveal [A08] Symbol Identification - paragraph missing initial double quote
14. Hai Reveal [A10] Demanding Satisfaction - extra space before period at end of sentence
15. Hai Reveal [A10] Demanding Satisfaction - corrected typo: "will" should be "well"
16. Hai Reveal [A12] Into the Lion's Den - bug in description: `<stopover>` instead of `<stopovers>`
17. Hai Reveal [A13-A] Unfettered Pickup - ships started in the wrong system
18. Hai Reveal [B01] Information Blackout - making the mission invisible prevented the player from knowing what to do next. Also, mission had the wrong completion condition.
19. Hai Reveal [B01-A] The Blockade Goes Up - corrected the confusing description
20. Hai Reveal [B01-A] The Blockade Goes Up - increased to 12 turns to allow more time for player to realize the ships are starting in distant systems and will need to refuel
21. Hai Reveal [B01-A] The Blockade Goes Up - incorrect offer condition
22. Hai Reveal [B01-A] The Blockade Goes Up - syndicate escorts were missing the "accompany" tag
23. Hai Reveal [B01-A] The Blockade Goes Up - gave more instructions when entering systems
24. Hai Reveal [B01-A] The Blockade Goes Up - added an "on visit" condition to inform player not all defending ships were destroyed
25. Hai Reveal [B03] Contact Giti - corrected typo: "too" instead of "to"
26. Hai Reveal [B04] The Road Not Taken - corrected paragraph indentation (must use tabs, not spaces)
27. Hai Reveal [B05-long] The Red Mystery - better description
28. Hai Reveal [B05-long] The Red Mystery - no completion condition, to ensure description remains until no longer relevant
29. Hai Reveal [B06-long] Tarazed Analysis - added a hint on where ships arrive most frequently
30. event "devil-run smugglers visible" - smugglers arrive more often. (Originally, the campaign had lots of ships in between far north and syndicate near the wormhole. Without them, there are few smugglers to find due to infrequent arrival times. This is confusing to players that don't know what to look for.)
31. Hai Reveal [B07-long] Learn of Keystones - corrected source and added a missing "fail" clause
32. Hai Reveal [B09] Scanning Devil-Hide - grammar error
33. Hai Reveal [B11] Moving Together - grammar error
34. Hai Reveal [B11] Moving Together - added an "on visit" to avoid confusing player
35. Hai Reveal [B12] Devil-Hide Battle - some ships lacked quantum keystones, so they could not reach Devil's Hide
36. Hai Reveal [B12] Devil-Hide Battle - More durable "npc save" ship designs. Ships that had to survive the battle could not reliably do so, due to too little shields. In particular, the Auxiliary, Dreadnought and Centipede frequently died. I tweaked their outfits and played through the battle a few times. If the player has a strong ship that does not use explosive ammo, the battle is quite playable.
37. Hai Reveal [B12] Devil-Hide Battle - autosave, and failure message. This is a hard battle if you don't know what to expect.
38. Hai Reveal [B13-G] Elenctic Guard - changed an incorrect mission description

### More Fixes

After resolving review comments and retesting, I found and fixed a few more bugs:

1. Hai Rescue: Yeertle Hint - does not vanish when Hai Leaks Response 6 cease to be active
2. Hai Rescue: Oonem Hint - does not vanish when Hai Leaks Response 6 cease to be active
3. Hai Rescue: Prison RP Hint - does not vanish when Hai Leaks Response 6 cease to be active
5. Hai Rescue: Meroot and Lucy Hint - does not vanish when Hai Leaks Response 6 cease to be active
6. Hai Reveal [B01-A] The Blockade Goes Up - does not always see the completion of A14, so I had to change its "to offer." The condition is functionally equivalent.
7. Hai Reveal [B02] Join the Fleet - "npc accompany" implies "npc save" so the mission is impossible if any of the escorts are killed. It is expected that some will die in the battle.
8. Hai Reveal [B02] Join the Fleet - "escort waiting" does nothing; it is the same as "escort." There is no way to make the NPC fleets wait to rendezvous with you at a specified system.
9. Hai Reveal [B02] Join the Fleet - fleets start far away, so they run out of fuel before they arrive. I've changed the mission so the fleets all start at Sunracer, in orbit of the player's planet.

### Yet More Fixes

A third set, after another round of review:

1. Better fixes from @MasterOfGrey for hai kidnapping victims missions.
2. Hai Reveal [A07] Deliver the Relays - workaround for a bug I can't fix. The relays remain in the ship after they'r

author: jontmy
body:
### Motivation

#114 and #117 are blocked by JCommander's (intentional) lack of support for global parameter validation, i.e. `add -t` and `add -m` are the same command, but our implementation splits them into two (or more) command classes.

### Changes

This PR introduces a "scope" for commands which are currently "task" (representing `-t`) and "module" (representing `-m`). I have deliberately avoided re-using `-t` and `-m` for scopes to reduce confusion.

This allows us to use command _phrases_ instead of command _words_, e.g. `add task` is the command phrase, whereas previously the command word was `add` and the option `-t` would define the scope.

As such we are free to split commands by their scope and continue to implement them in separate classes, thereby unblocking #114 and #117.

### Example

`add -t` which used to be a single `add` command can be separated into their `AddTaskCommand` and `AddModuleCommand` classes using the command phrases `add task` and `add module` respectively.

Note that you'll need to register both commands with JCommander in `ModtrektParser` independently.

### RFC

I'm leaving this PR open as a draft until the meeting tonight in case we don't go forward with this.

--

**BREAKING CHANGE: this breaks every command which uses `-t` or `-m`.**

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

Implemented `select` entities for:
- Selecting week profile for a zone.
- Overriding preset for all zones (global override).

Selecting week profile is useful for a workaround  to turn all heaters in a zone to off, which can only be done via a week profile (auto mode). author: cston
body:
Split out ref safety analysis into a separate pass after binding.

Local scopes and scopes for placeholder nodes are no longer calculated during binding and stored on the corresponding `SourceLocalSymbol` or `BoundNode`. Instead, all scopes are calculated in the visitor. That represents the bulk of this change.

Otherwise, the PR has minimal changes to the current ref safety analysis code, beyond moving the code into a new `RefSafetyAnalysis` visitor type. In particular, analysis is still split across `Get` and `Check` methods, and split across `Val` and `Ref` methods, and those methods are called from various `Visit` methods in the visitor, in some cases more than once. We can consider merging those code paths with the `Visit` methods in subsequent PRs.

See https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/63897.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

This makes it follow what was decided in [Bug #19055]:

* `Regexp.new(str, timeout: nil)` should respect the global timeout
* `Regexp.new(str, timeout: huge_val)` should use the maximum value that can be represented in the internal representation
* `Regexp.new(str, timeout: 0 or negative value)` should raise an error

author: wiktor-k
body:
Adds safe interface for parsing and constructing DSA signatures and their components: `r` and `s`.

This mirrors the interface offered by `EcdsaSig` with one omission: there is no `sign` method on `DsaSig` (as in `EcdsaSig`) since [`DSA_do_sign`](https://www.openssl.org/docs/manmaster/man3/DSA_do_sign.html) seems to be deprecated.

author: sprintaway
body:
Adds in functionality to support commands such as `loan 2 2` which automatically adds in a return date of 14 days from today (which is "saved" properly in that it is a fixed date and does not get deleted after closing and reopening. In particular, there is a json property of returnDate that is set to null if the book is not loaned, and a json property of isLoaned that copies the book 
isLoaned)

Commands such as `loan 2 2 tomorrow`, `loan 2 2 2023-08-08`, or even `loan 2 2 sometime next sunday i guess` also works properly through `PrettyTimeParser` library and sets the return date respectively instead of adding 14 days from today.
(Note that it looks through by order and can only accept one date however, `loan 2 2 tomorrow or next sunday` sets the return date to tomorrow and not next sunday)

When an invalid command such as `loan 2 2 somewhere` is entered, "Unable to parse as date." is displayed on UI. 
(Thanks Parth for helping with the loan saving issue last time!)

KNOWN ISSUES:

~~Severe saving issues.~~

MAJOR ISSUE: 
- [x] ~~Does not save books that are available after closing 
and reopening app, only saves books that are loaned out.~~

MODERATE ISSUE: 
- [x] ~~After adding books, the command box no longer 
updates properly.~~

MINOR ISSUES:
- [x] ~~Sometimes loan date does not update automatically, 
have to select it to force it to refresh.~~
- [x] ~~Under user list, a user's loaned book list should contain the 
return by: date as well.~~
- [x] ~~Error messages related to loan command should be updated to better reflect librarian's errors.~~
- [ ] There is a _minor_ noticeable delay that is caused by the loan command, presumably due to inefficient loops or parsing.

Resolves #151

# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: rageknify
body:
Currently we run 7 different jobs:
- tests linux
- tests macos
- tests windows
- rustfmt
- clippy
- examples
- documentation

With this change I reduced them to 4 and hopefully sped them up.

The total execution time is limited by the tests, especially linux that calculates coverage. Having separate jobs for clippy and rustfmt (which take a very small amount of time) is a waste of energy.
With this PR:
Introduced a new cargo profile, `ci`, that should create smaller sized binaries and reduce the our cache usage.
I changed the test runner for macos and windows to [nextest](https://nexte.st/), which should be faster and is specifically designed for CI.
I merged all smaller tasks in a single job, misc, the steps clearly identify what is being tested so it shouldn't affect clarity.
Switched to using the [rust-cache](https://github.com/Swatinem/rust-cache) GH action, this simplifies our work by no longer having to worry about which directories to cache, rust-cache handles all that for us.

~~The bors task should also be modified, I'll get to it as soon as I have time. I believe it should be possible for us to have a single workflow described and have it both be the normal CI and the bors test.~~

body: The idea is to sort the intervals in increasing order of their starting time. Then create an empty stack and for each interval, If the stack is empty or the top interval in the stack does not overlap with the current interval, push it into the stack. If the top interval of the stack overlaps with the current interval, merge both intervals by updating the end of the top interval at the ending of the current interval. Finally, print all non-overlapping intervals present in the stack.

author: richardkoehler
body:
With this PR I propose multiple but rather minor changes (no changes to the way py_neuromodulation works or is structured):

- First I made some minor changes to the tests, in order to make pytest run without error (in testing classes, pytest does not allow an `__init__` method)
- The tests gave a pandas deprecation warning (related to ``df.append()``), which I now circumvent by first appending to a list and only at the end creating the dataframe. This should also be faster and more memory-efficient. The tests still run through smoothly.
- Finally, I moved setup information for pip into the `pyproject.toml` file, which is now the new accepted standard and which most libraries (like black, pylint etc.) also support. I also added some metadata about py_neuromodulation to the `pyproject.toml` file, you can just check it out and add or change anything else.
- You will notice the version of py_neuromodulation is retrieved dynamically from the py_neuromodulation ``__init__.py`` file (this way the ``__version__`` attribute in the py_neuromodulation package and the pip package always match up. I gave it the version number ``0.1.0.dev1`` for the moment, since it is still under development, but feel free to change anything :)
- All requirements for the pip installation are in the ``pyproject.toml`` file, and I added all requirements that were needed for the tests. But I might have missed some other requirements, since the tests currently don't cover all of the modules.
- **Edit:** I noticed black also did some formatting on ``nm_analysis``. But the only relevant changes are those made from lines 895 onward.

@timonmerk I would love to hear your feedback on this. You can try it out by running the following commands:
```
conda create -n pynm-test python=3.10
conda activate pynm-test
```
Navigate to the clone of py_neuromodulation.
```
pip install .[dev]
pytest -v .
```
All tests should optimally run without error.

For editable development mode just do:
```
pip install -e .[dev]
```

#### Highlights

Flux v0.36.0 comes with new features and improvements. Users are encouraged to upgrade for the best experience.

-   Verify OCI Helm charts signed by Cosign (including keyless) with [HelmChart.spec.verify](https://fluxcd.io/docs/cheatsheets/oci-artifacts/#verify-helm-charts).

-   The kustomize-controller memory usage was reduced by 90% when performing artifact operations.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: kashifkhan
body:
**Whats Happening**


We are raising a `TimeoutError` in websocket transport read [here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/blob/c3dbace352eb4ed5c3c4c17b737620ac3cda0c9e/sdk/eventhub/azure-eventhub/azure/eventhub/_pyamqp/_transport.py#L726). This error bubbles up and gets caught by `receive_frame` in `transport` [here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/blob/c3dbace352eb4ed5c3c4c17b737620ac3cda0c9e/sdk/eventhub/azure-eventhub/azure/eventhub/_pyamqp/_transport.py#L468). As you can see the error gets squashed here as we treat `TimeoutErrors` as an empty frame. This is exactly why we never enter the re-connect loop as the error doesnt bubble up further. If one raises from `receive_frame` things work properly and a re-connect loop is started


**What was I seeing yesterday**

Throwing an `OSError` or `ConnectionError` ( also an OSError ) causes the chain of error handling to work properly and enter the reconnect loop.


**Why dont we see this on socket connections?**

[`socket.timeout`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/socket.html#socket.timeout) is an `OSError`, it used to be `TimeoutError` and hence the problem doesnt show there as it propagates up.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: shaman123
body:
## Motivation

#8392 
#8297 types are complex. That introduced the need to test typing, see comments.
I worked on types. And then I had to test it comes out as I expected it.
So I found myself writing calls to the animate function to see if I wrote the complex type correctly. 
Instead of writing and deleting why not have a dedicated place that I can work on, comment and discuss in a PR and make sure it behaves as I expect it to.
Then, regardless, I found that the entry point to the repo is not typed. A good case for why ts tests are crucial.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34343793/197469717-211ec232-b747-41d3-b177-2e2d5781958e.png)


## Research
- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49296151/how-to-write-tests-for-typescript-typing-definition:
  - suggests `dtslint`, `tsd`, see below
  - suggests using `// @ts-expect-error` and test if the file compiles.
  - refers to how [express tests TS](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/master/types/express/express-tests.ts)
- https://github.com/Microsoft/dtslint => `@definitelytyped/dtslint`
suggested by official TS but has limitation since it does a string comparison of the compiler returned type so `a | b != b | a` and typos in test files will f*** us over
Seems to run only on declaration files so is completely worthless
- https://github.com/SamVerschueren/tsd
js test suite with `expectType`, `expectError` etc., suggested by official TS
Can only assert a value, not params. so is worthless on its own
- https://github.com/mmkal/expect-type
js test suite, seems not popular yet
- https://github.com/dsherret/conditional-type-checks
type assertions + js assertions, looks good
- https://github.com/JoshuaKGoldberg/eslint-plugin-expect-type
unrelated to testing

## Findings

- use `// @ts-expect-error explanation` to assert an error and test for file compilation
- `conditional-type-checks` | `tsd` => `conditional-type-checks` wins since it is more flexible and accurate (see playground below) and allows testing function parameters and whatever
- `@definitelytyped/dtslint` is useless

author: easbar
body:
Apparently setting `"jsx": "react-jsx"` instead of `"jsx": "react"` in tsconfig.json is now the way to go: https://reactjs.org/blog/2020/09/22/introducing-the-new-jsx-transform.html#whats-different-in-the-new-transform

For us it means we no longer need to explicitly `import React` in `.tsx` files, which was a bit annoying because for example IntelliJ did not detect this as error and we only noticed when running the app, for example we got:

```
[tsl] ERROR in /home/me/code/routing/graphhopper/gh-maps-react/src/sidebar/search/AddressInputAutocomplete.tsx(132,10)
      TS2686: 'React' refers to a UMD global, but the current file is a module. Consider adding an import instead.
```

author: javanna
body:
Reverts elastic/elasticsearch#90951

In hindsight, there is a slight possibility that existing users are relying on Elasticsearch accepting field names that contain only dots when subobjects are disabled. The original change assumed that such fields were not accepted in mappings, but they actually are, as #90950 has surfaced. As a result, we end up rejecting field names that the mappings would happily accept, which is inconsistent.

author: leppert
body:
This PR creates better separation between the three core elements of mischief:
- Crawling: the process of interacting with a page
- Interception: the process of observing and capturing the traffic generated via crawling
- Exporting: the process of saving the intercepted traffic in a format that can later be replayed

Additional notes:
- I envision Exchanges to map to Interceptors and provide a standardized interface from the Interceptor's format to what can later be used by Exporters. As a result, a little bit of data munging that was happening in `warc.js` has been moved into MischiefProxyExchange.js (ex: headers being converted to a map)

Open questions:
- Should we be using the `Mischief` prefix on classes? Not sure what best practices are these days but we should be consistent (Exchanges use them right now whereas Interceptors and Exporters don't)

author: jgutman
body:
### Intent

Addresses #11693

### Approach

For Mac Electron package builds, the path to the rpostback executable is: `RStudio.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/rpostback`
However the path to the rpostback-askpass executable is:
`RStudio.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/postback/rpostback-askpass`

Similarly, for Windows Electron package builds, the path to the rpostback executable is:
`C:/Program Files/RStudio/resources/app/bin/rpostback`
However the path to the rpostback-askpass executable is:
`C:/Program Files/RStudio/resources/app/bin/postback/rpostback-askpass`

So what we need to do is fix the path for `rpostback-askpass` relative to `rpostback` in non-development builds.
We do this by taking the rpostback path, getting its parent, adding the `/postback` to that parent path, and adding that directory to the path. This way the RS_RPOSTBACK_PATH environment variable is set correctly, and the `bin/postback` folder containing the `rpostback-askpass` is added to the system path so we can find the askpass executable

### QA Notes
Needs to be retested on at least Windows and Mac, and with both password protected and non-password protected SSH keys. Be sure to clear out `~/.ssh/known_hosts` and start with a fresh SSH key as that seemed to impact testing

body:
Add a test case to feature_taproot which involves an output that is (incorrectly) constructed, using an invalid internal public key and valid script tree. It is designed to detect cases where the script path spending validation logic does not detect this case, and instead treats the internal public key as the point at infinity.

Equivalent unit test case added in https://github.com/bitcoin-core/qa-assets/pull/98.

author: carleyjmartin
body:
# Scope 

pyDARN release branch for v3.1 includes the following features:
- Full Cartopy coastline plotting options for all spatial plots
  - **NEW** `coastline` keyword in method calls
- Full Cartopy integration for plotting in geographic coordinates for grid and fan plots
- Completed polar coordinate convection maps including reference vector and many customization options
- Improved ACF plotting
- New `HALF_SLANT` range estimation for RTP
- **Bug fix** Multiple fan plots now available on one axis
- **Bug fix** `lowlat` keyword now available for geographic coordinate plots
- **Bug fix** Colorbars now extend/don't extend as required
along with many other minor improvements and bug fixes!

There is a PR not yet merged for the latitude and longitude y-axis options for RTPs, this is not vital but if you are interested in having this released alongside this release, please test that first and I can get it in here.

There is also updates to the documentation. To see those changes check out the read the docs here: https://pydarn.readthedocs.io/en/develop/

## Approval

**Number of approvals:** 3 or more, code review and testing for release
**DEADLINE: ~~21st NOV~~ 25th NOV**

## Test
**Note testers: please indicate what version of matplotlib you are using** - incredibly important as this branch includes a depreciation for matplotlib!

Please test as much as you can but especially:
- Grid plots (geographic, polar, coastlines)
- Fan plots (geo/polar, coastlines)
- Convection plots (polar only, all peripherials work, coastlines)
- ACF plots (new keywords and subplots)
- Range estimations in RTPs
- NEW CHANGE FROM REVIEWS - test read_hdw_files function.
- **Check you are on the zenodo json where you expect and with the correct information, let me know if there are any issues**

Please ask if you require any specific data formats to test!

author: thadeucity
body:
Improve the performance of the `tint` and `shade` functions.

It is a tiny performance improvement and lib size reduction, but it does not degrade in any shape or form the quality of the code, so I believe it is a welcome change.

The improvement is achieved by exiting the `parseToRgb` function in the first `IF` that checks for `HEX Colors`, this way not testing or matching the default color unnecessarily.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: paulrberg
body:
## Rationale

In the previous PR, @andreivladbrg used the `_safeMint` function to mint the NFTs in our `create` functions. But this is not quite right, because it means that smart contract wallet recipients like Gnosis Safe won't be able to receive streams (since they don't implement the [`IERC721receiver`][ierc721-receiver] interface). This is a big no-no.

This PR changes the function to `_mint`, which does not check for the receiver interface. And this is fine because:

1. Smart contract wallets can still transfer NFTs (see explanation [here][se])
2. Those contract which cannot transfer NFTs can presumably still interact with Sablier, otherwise the sender wouldn't have created the stream with them as `recipient`. And if they can interact with Sablier, they can cancel and withdraw from the stream.

Our protocol is first and foremost a streaming service, and only second an NFT project. The NFT is there only to give us interoperability with the outer DeFi ecosystem.

Separately, this PR also changes the tests to use `transferFrom` function instead of `safeTransferFrom`, since the latter is not needed for EOAs (and it's only EOAs that we use in our tests).

## Changelog:

- [x] refactor: use "_mint" instead of "_safeMint"
- [x] test: use "transferFrom" instead of "safeTransferFrom"

[ierc721-receiver]: https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/2.x/api/token/erc721#IERC721Receiver
[se]: https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/questions/124516/safetransferfrom-of-erc721-not-working-when-transfering-nft-to-a-safe-address

author: misberner
body:
## Description

gRPC code generation generates `Unimplemented...` structs that return an unimplemented status code for all methods. This struct should be embedded in all gRPC service implementations. While this is not currently enforced, future gRPC code generator versions will make this mandatory (this behavior can be disabled, but it is not recommended; see [here](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/3669) for a lengthy discussion on this matter with the clear verdict that gRPC authors see embedding of `Unimplemented..` as something that should always have been required).

Alas, this makes service type assertions ineffective, but that seems to be the pill to swallow.

author: zacharylowell
body:
## Describe problem solved by this pull request
This PR is meant to allow for PX4_INFO and other logging functions (err, warn, etc.) to be used by qurt and to be outputted onto mini-dm -- FUTURE will require string being passed into PX4_INFO to be sent over to apps side to be printed out by px4 shell.

## Describe your solution
Implemented a qurt_logger that leverages a hex function called HAP_debug - this function is in charge of printing out strings on mini-dm. This was then abstracted out to a function called qurt_log which was then leveraged in log.h.

## Describe possible alternatives
Currently this is the best possible route. Only other implementation that needs to happen is for these strings to be sent over to the apps side via a uorb communicator which would then be printed out on PX4 shell.

## Test data / coverage
This was tested using mini-dm and the muorb protobuf code base that runs on the slpi.

author: vanvoljg
body:
Including the start metadata in the stop metadata for `:telemetry.span`-wrapped Elasticsearch calls. This makes it so reporters don't have to retain requests for an entire span and can use only the `:stop` event to work with metrics.

It also locks `sigaws_otp_24`, because that was missing previously.

For context, see this issue in the Telemetry repo: https://github.com/beam-telemetry/telemetry/issues/112#issuecomment-1289521937

Specifcially, I'm adding these changes because it seems like upstream Telemetry doesn't feel like it's the correct choice to do this automatically. This implies that libraries which implement Telemetry must do this on their own--include StartMetadata along with StopMetadata whenever possible--and, hence, this PR.

author: mjlshen
body:
### What type of PR is this?
feature

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Per OSD-13536, `KubeDaemonsetMisScheduled` commonly manifests as a low alert because `openshift-dns/dns-default` pods get scheduled onto infra nodes before their taints get applied. We have this SOP: https://github.com/openshift/ops-sop/blob/master/v4/alerts/KubeDaemonSetMisScheduled.md which directs SREs to this handy script: https://github.com/openshift/ops-sop/blob/master/v4/utils/misscheduled_ds.sh which does this for the SRE.

However, by just putting this script into this osd-rebalance-infra-nodes CronJob, we can periodically check if there are any misscheduled dns-default pods and delete the ones running on infra nodes.

body:
- This PR adds two env variable options, to both cache and use cached builds of a build dir during a rebuild.
- The self-explanatory ENV variables are `CREW_CACHE_BUILD` and `CREW_CACHE_FAILED_BUILD`.
- The builds are only cached if the `CREW_CACHE_ENABLED` environment variable also exists.
- Later we could modify this to pick up existing cached builds to be used for other packages. (e.g. have a `gcc_libs` and `gcc_binaries` package which both use the cached build for `gcc`)
- Note that you need a package file which can handle build directories already existing. e.g.
```
  def self.build
    FileUtils.mkdir_p 'builddir'
    Dir.chdir 'builddir' do
      unless File.file?('build.ninja')
        system "cmake \
          -G Ninja \
          #{CREW_CMAKE_OPTIONS} \
          -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON \
          -DNATIVE=OFF \
          .."
      end
    end
    system 'ninja -C builddir'
  end
```

author: bugfood
body:
When `pdk bundle exec rake litmus:acceptance:parallel` is run twice, the second command hangs. This happens because ssh-keygen is waiting for interactive input:
```
/home/testuser-ssh/.ssh/id_rsa already exists.
Overwrite (y/n)?
```

To fix this, ensure that we start out with an empty .ssh directory each time.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: dnivra
body:
Sometimes unicorn triggers read hook multiple times for a single read in an instruction(eg: when reading 16 bytes from memory). If the first partial read is symbolic, then we map all values read so far to VEX statements in the current block where they are read and then wait until the remaining bytes have been read. However, we do not update some state data used by the taint engine to correctly resume taint propagation after a memory read is completed. This cause the second partial read hook to incorrectly assume this is first time symbolic bytes are being read from memory and it will attempt to remap all memory reads to the corresponding VEX statements in the current block(which was already done completed in the previous read hook). This PR fixes this by setting the required data so that the taint engine correctly resumes taint propagation from where it stopped previously.

I do not have a test case for this since the issue was discovered using some code that cannot be made public now. If needed, I could attempt creating a test case.

author: banool
body: ### Description As it is now, if you run this command and the node thread panics, it just prints the panic without exiting. Worse than that, if it returns an error, it prints nothing at all and just silently sits there, broken. ``` cargo run -p aptos -- node run-local-testnet --force-restart --assume-yes ``` This PR fixes that, making sure that the CLI exists if the local testnet / faucet exit. This is a very imperfect fix. Really what we want is something like what we do in the tap: https://github.com/aptos-labs/aptos-tap/blob/main/src/server/run.rs#L170. In this setup, all never-ending tasks are represented as futures (whereas this is a blend of future and blocking thread) and all tasks return errors, so instead of printing the error and then bubbling up a `()`, it actually returns the error, which can then get propagated all the way up to main. ### Test Plan Command: ``` cargo run -p aptos -- node run-local-testnet --force-restart --config-path /tmp/yes_api.yaml --assume-yes ``` No error introduced: ``` Completed generating configuration: Log file: "/Users/dport/a/core/.aptos/testnet/validator.log" Test dir: "/Users/dport/a/core/.aptos/testnet" Aptos root key path: "/Users/dport/a/core/.aptos/testnet/mint.key" Waypoint: 0:0d22c659f2a6e918612c9be311a0efdfa1fc9cf9751a4968f866924faf73bb9b ChainId: testing REST API endpoint: http://0.0.0.0:8080 Metrics endpoint: http://0.0.0.0:9102/metrics Aptosnet Fullnode network endpoint: /ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/6184 Aptos is running, press ctrl-c to exit ``` Error introduced in the node thread: ``` Node stopped unexpectedly Err( "manual error", ) { "Error": "Unexpected error: One of the components stopped unexpectedly" } ``` Panic introduced in the faucet future. Output: https://gist.github.com/banool/c6b4392aa1f41e9fb4f22c6a6b839a8c. - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/aptos-labs/aptos-core/5261)

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The Kubelet's read-only port (customarily 10255) can be overridden via config file or command line. However, the bind address for the readonly server is always the same as the secure serving address.

It may be useful to restrict the read-only port to the loopback interface, but there is no way to do so independently of the secure serving address.

Add a config item and flag to control the readonly address. Defaults to the secure serving address if not set.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

WIP. Needs updates to tests, kubeadm, etc.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

-->
```release-note

Add a new flag and field to KubeletConfiguration that allows setting the readonly port bind address independently of the
secure server address. 

New flag: --read-only-bind-address.
KubeletConfiguration item: ReadOnlyBindAddress. 

The value of --read-only-bind-address defaults to the server bind address (`--server`) if not set. 

The readonly bind address is only used if the read only server is enabled by setting --read-only-port != 0.
```

author: rouson
body: This PR ensures that the `check_specification_expression()` function in the `compiler_test_m` module recognizes and is able to invoke the IBM XL Fortran compile using `execute_command_line` subroutine, which is required because the only standard-conforming way to observe type finalization in a specification expression is through error termination (because the final subroutine must be `pure` and therefore can't do I/O).

author: billyoneal
body:
I have observed many people tend to "tune out" our current pull request template, including maintainers, who don't even look at the content and sometimes miss important things people are trying to tell us. To that end, I would like to replace it with something more useful, including things for people submitting the most common kinds of PRs to check.

-----------------------------------------

Port update checklist:

- [ ] Changes comply with the [maintainer guide](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/docs/maintainers/maintainer-guide.md)
- [ ] SHA512s are updated for each updated download
- [ ] The "supports" clause reflects platforms that may be fixed by this new version
- [ ] Any fixed [CI baseline](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/scripts/ci.baseline.txt) entries are removed from that file.
- [ ] Any patches that are no longer applied are deleted from the port's directory.
- [ ] The version database is fixed by rerunning `./vcpkg x-add-version --all` and committing the result.
- [ ] Only one version is added to each modified port's versions file.

-----------------------------------------

New port checklist:

- [ ] Changes comply with the [maintainer guide](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/docs/maintainers/maintainer-guide.md)
- [ ] The name of the port matches an existing name for this component on https://repology.org/ if possible, and/or is strongly associated with that component on search engines.
- [ ] Optional dependencies are resolved in exactly one way. For example, if the component is built with CMake, all `find_package` calls are REQUIRED, are satisfied by `vcpkg.json`'s declared dependencies, or disabled with [CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_Xxx](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/variable/CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_PackageName.html)
- [ ] The versioning scheme in `vcpkg.json` matches what upstream says.
- [ ] The license declaration in `vcpkg.json` matches what upstream says.
- [ ] The installed as the "copyright" file matches what upstream says.
- [ ] The source code of the component installed comes from an authoritative source.
- [ ] The generated "usage text" is accurate. See docs/examples/adding-an-explicit-usage.md for context.
- [ ] The version database is fixed by rerunning `./vcpkg x-add-version --all` and committing the result.
- [ ] Only one version is in the new port's versions file.
- [ ] Only one version is added to each modified port's versions file.
